title: Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Digital Television Switch-over) Bill 2008
portfolio: Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

divisions.question: Bill—by leave—taken as a whole. Nick Minchin by leave—I move opposition amendments (1) to (3) on sheet 5665-revised together: (1) Schedule 2, page 4 (after line 13), after item 3, insert: 3A Clause 2 of Schedule 4 Insert: **_minimum analog switch-off readiness criteria_** has the meaning given by clause 5G. (2) Schedule 2, page 5 (after line 32), after item 4, insert: 4A At the end of Part 1 of Schedule 4 Add: 5G Minimum analog switch-off readiness criteria (1) The Minister must, by legislative instrument, determine **_minimum analog switch-off readiness criteria_**. (2) The Minister must make a determination under subclause (1) within 6 months of the day on which this Act receives the Royal Assent. (3) A determination made under subclause (1) must include criteria against which the television broadcasting services in each local market area can be objectively assessed, to determine whether the following objectives can be met: (a) that the transmission of broadcasting services should achieve the same level of coverage and potential reception quality after digital television switch-over as was achieved by the transmission of those service in that area prior to switch-over; and (b) that all households which received free to air television coverage in analog mode should be able to receive the same level of coverage after switch-over; and (c) that adequate measures have been taken to assist household readiness for analog switch-off, as indicated by household take-up of equipment capable of receiving digital terrestrial free to air television transmission and awareness of analog switch-off and of methods to convert to digital. Assessment against readiness criteria (4) In relation to each local market area determined under paragraph 5F(1)(a), the Minister must cause a report to be prepared assessing the local market area against the minimum analog switch-off readiness criteria. That the committee agrees to the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the bill.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: Moved the introduction of two bills: one to amend broadcasting law and another to amend migration law, at the request of Senators Conroy and Chris Evans.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Digital Television Switch-over) Bill 2008 set a staggered region-by-region digital switch-over timetable to be completed by 31 December 2013, with the Minister determining local market areas and switch-over dates. The Migration Legislation Amendment (Worker Protection) Bill 2008 introduced a new sponsorship framework for temporary skilled visas with better-defined obligations, expanded investigation powers, and civil penalties of up to $6,600 for individuals and $33,000 for bodies corporate.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The report on the Broadcasting Legislation Amendment (Digital Television Switch-over) Bill 2008 was presented to the Senate, with proceedings and documents included.

speeches.speaker: Nick Minchin
speeches.brief: The coalition supported the Digital Television Switch-over Bill 2008 but moved amendments requiring public readiness criteria and black spot identification before analog switch-off, arguing the government’s 2013 deadline risked leaving viewers without digital signals, especially in regional areas. The coalition also criticised the government for lacking specific take-up benchmarks and funding for disadvantaged consumers, community broadcasters, and transmission upgrades.

speeches.speaker: Nick Minchin
speeches.brief: The opposition moved three amendments to require the minister to set and publish minimum analog switch-off readiness criteria, assess each local market area against them, and report quarterly on digital transmission infrastructure and black spots. The government opposed amendments (1) and (2), arguing they would remove key incentives for broadcasters and undermine the switch-over deadline, while the Greens supported only amendment (3) on black spot reporting. The Senate agreed to amendments (1)–(2) and (3) separately, amending the bill accordingly.

The House of Representatives returned the bill with amendments requiring the ACMA to prepare quarterly reports on digital television conversion objectives and the Minister to report every six months on self-help re-transmission services and blackspots.

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: The Coalition accepted government amendments (1) and (3) on digital switch-off readiness criteria but rejected amendments (2), (4), (5), (6), and (7), insisting on its own quarterly reporting requirements for digital black spots starting 1 April 2009. Senator Minchin warned that if Mildura and rural South Australia are not ready for analog switch-off, the Coalition will move to disallow the minister's legislative instrument.
